final.reason: Exhausted all 6 physical evaluations across main length 24-42mm, aux 17.5-18mm, C=80-150uF, gate=2.0-2.9V, and threshold=0.15-0.55V. Every design gave pass_=false, faults=4, delivered_on_time=0, false_reports=0, with all mechanical slacks <1 (stress 0.90-0.94, travel 0.92-0.98), so no safety violation but zero deliveries. Critically, the outcome was invariant to storage capacitance, gate voltage, and to LOWERING the comparator threshold through 0.15-0.55V; main length only shifted stress/travel. This pattern strongly indicates the analog comparator threshold sits BELOW the .8g/250Hz nuisance envelope (aux response roughly 0.6-0.7V), so the nuisance repeatedly wakes/drains the node (the 4 faults), while the .5g/210Hz target envelope (~3V) could be separated by a threshold near 0.7-1.0V. That high-threshold region (and its interaction with a background-resonant main beam for energy) is the leading candidate but was untested within budget. No design was verified to pass, and a failed search is not a full-domain proof, so I cannot assert INFEASIBLE; no final design can be honestly selected.
